verificationWarning: PARTLY VERIFIED, AND STILL NOT YOUR PRICE. 28 of 44 entries were checked in September 2026 against Microsoft's published pricing, including the 1 July 2026 increase; 2 is inferred from a parent SKU; 14 remain unchecked seed data, mostly the standalone Defender components, for which Microsoft withdrew public per-seat pricing. Every entry carries its own $confidence and $source. Whatever the confidence, these are public list prices and WILL be wrong for any customer on an EA, MCA or CSP agreement. Supply negotiated rates via -CustomPricing, or price SKUs inline in the app. The report always states which basis produced its figures.
securityValueShareNote: securityValueShare is the fraction of a SKU's price this tool attributes to its security-bearing capabilities. It is this tool's allocation model, not a Microsoft-published figure, because no vendor publishes 'the Safe Links portion of an E5 seat'. It feeds the security budget in the exports and nothing else. When Microsoft changes a SKU's price or contents, the share is re-derived rather than carried: the security dollars from before the change are kept, and the price change is split across what was added in proportion to each addition's standalone list price, weighted by how much of it is security (1.0 for a security product, 0.5 for device and app management, 0 for support, analytics and productivity). Additions with no per-seat price cannot enter that split and are named instead. An entry's $shareBasis shows its arithmetic. Holding a share fixed through a price increase credits security with part of every increase, including increases that bought storage or productivity features, which is the drift the October 2026 retune corrected. Override per SKU as needed.

prices.$note: Microsoft 365 E7. Launched 1 May 2026 at a USD 99 list price per user per month on an annual term. E7 bundles E5, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Agent 365 and the Entra Suite. securityValueShare is derived rather than published: E5 contributes 0.4 of USD 60.00, which is USD 24.00, and the Entra Suite adds roughly USD 12.00 of identity and network security, so roughly a third of the USD 99 is security bearing. Copilot and Agent 365 are not. That is this tool's allocation model and a consultant should override it when the customer disagrees.
prices.$source: Widely reported at USD 99 list (Directions on Microsoft, SAMexpert, Valorem Reply). Not confirmed against a Microsoft-published price page.

$perEntryProvenanceNote: Entries carry $note, $source, $confidence and $asOf. Keys beginning with $ are documentation and are stripped before the engine reads the file, so provenance can live beside a price without changing the runtime schema. $confidence is verified (checked against a Microsoft page), reasoned (derived from a related SKU, with the derivation stated) or unverified (seed data carried forward because no public figure was found). $asOf is when that entry was last checked, which is why an unverified entry still reads 2025-01 while the file reads 2026-09.
